title: Computerised Method of Multiparameter Optimisation of Predictive Control Algorithms for Asynchronous Electric Drives
content: This article is devoted to solving the scientific and technical problem of increasing the energy efficiency of electromechanical systems driven by asynchronous electric drives, which is an important task in industry, transport and energy in the context of sustainable development and rational use of resources. Due to the large number of drives, energy efficient operation is increasingly important in drive control. In this context, one of the promising areas is the application of a predictive control strategy that allows for reducing energy losses in dynamic modes of electric drives. For a systematic parametrisation of such algorithms, this paper proposes a computerised method for multiparameter optimisation of predictive control algorithms for asynchronous electric drives. In the course of the study of this article, a computer model was built in Matlab & Simulink based on the gradient-based model predictive control strategy. A series of simulation experiments were carried out with variation of the sampling step, number of iterations, prediction horizon, loss function parameters and maximum linear search step to identify their impact on the control quality indicators. For the multicriteria optimisation a taxonomic approach is proposed. The study results show that the optimal setting of the algorithmic parameters improves the accuracy of task pro-cessing, reduces energy consumption and reduces computation time. The results obtained can be used to design and operate energy-efficient control systems for asynchronous electric drives in industrial and transport applications. Prospects for further research include the development of hybrid intelligent architectures to increase the adaptability of predictive control and its integration into automated control systems.
